title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when traffic congestion prevented them from reaching charging locations and depleted their batteries. At least a dozen vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, were left stationary following fireworks near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the outage to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion.

This is a deployment failure in route planning and energy management. The system was used during an event with traffic conditions outside normal operating parameters, and vehicles lacked sufficient battery reserves or alternative instructions to handle the extended idle time. A human dispatcher with authority to reroute vehicles or preemptively move them before gridlock formed could have prevented the stranding. The incident also revealed a separate safety concern when at least one vehicle continued driving near active fireworks and another caught fire after driving over fireworks debris, though no injuries occurred.

It is not established whether Waymo's dispatch system had visibility into the Fourth of July event's traffic impact in advance, or what decision processes determined whether vehicles should have been taken offline before the celebrations.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Some vehicles required towing, and Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear them from the roadways.

The incident prompted safety concerns among passengers and frustration from stranded motorists. One passenger reported a Waymo vehicle continued driving while fireworks exploded nearby, and another vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries occurred. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the traffic situation with public and private partners to improve future event management. This incident follows a similar December outage when over 100,000 Waymo users experienced service disruptions during a citywide power failure.
